releaseBranch.description: Optional. The branch a release PR targets. releaseChecklist `when.release: true` matches only when the PR's actual base equals it; unset, such items never match (PREFLIGHT says so).

mergeAuthority.description: Who merges. none: the kit never merges, it hands over a mergeable PR and stops at G12 (G13 runs when the user reports or the host shows the merge). per-pr (default): the user's go per PR; a standing grant from the user's words is allowed with scope cycle only. standing: a standing grant may also have scope session.

envProbe.description: Command(s) that check whether this nature's test dependencies are actually reachable in THIS environment — a DB liveness ping, a container-daemon check, a health curl. PREFLIGHT runs it while capturing the baseline (§Stage 0.5). A FAILING probe is one of the two pieces of evidence a quarantine needs; the other is the suite's OWN startup error, and neither alone qualifies — this proves the environment is missing something, never which suites needed it, so one failed probe never licenses quarantining a second suite. A PASSING probe is a hard bar: nothing under this nature may be quarantined for that dependency. If it passes and a suite still cannot start (an ephemeral or container-provisioned dependency this ping never touched), that is a DIFFERENT dependency — probe that one, or leave the suite in its stricter category. Quarantined suites are recorded in state.baseline.unrunnableHere and gates G6/G9 diff AROUND them: neither a regression nor coverage, with sc-ship mapping any criterion they alone cover to review-only (ci-deferred) on the pre-merge manual gate. Deliberately narrow: a suite that starts and fails is a failure, and one that starts and skips itself (@Disabled, zero-executed, DDL/seed/auth not provisioned) stays a FAIL/deferral per 0.2.23.

ciBaseline.description: Where this nature's suite runs in CI, so PREFLIGHT can take the baseline from the base commit's own CI run instead of running the suite locally (§Stage 0.5, docs/test-baseline.md). `job` names the CI job/check that runs the same selection as `tests`; `report` names the artifact holding its machine-readable report (JUnit XML, runner JSON). With the report, state.baseline.source = ci and the failing set is read from it; without it, ci-status-only, where any failure in a suite this cycle runs blocks. Host-agnostic: any CI that exposes a run's commit, conclusion and artifacts qualifies.

coverage.description: How gate G6 measures core LINE coverage for this nature from a report file, never stdout. The full rule — path matching and the counted element per format, the baseline-relative floor, undetermined and ci-deferred outcomes — is in sc-implement G6. Omit it and G6 records `n/a: no coverage config`.

command.description: Run as its own step; must (re)write reportPath.

reportPath.description: Repo-relative path of the report the command writes.

format.description: istanbul-json = coverage-summary.json. other = no built-in reading; the extraction method is recorded in state.

corePaths.description: Globs over the normalised repo-relative source path of each report entry.

sourceRoots.description: Prefixes for report paths given relative — needed for jacoco, whose report carries package + file name only.

ciReport.description: The CI job and artifact holding this coverage report: a source for the base measurement when it cannot run locally, and the concrete item named on the pre-merge manual gate when G6 coverage is ci-deferred.

threshold.description: Percent. At or above it G6 coverage passes; below it, only a measured base can still pass it (sc-implement G6).

releaseSmoke.description: Per nature: the release-artifact smoke gate G9 requires when the diff touches appliesTo. Full rule: sc-qa — Release-artifact smoke.

appliesTo.description: Globs whose change triggers the smoke: build config, shrinker/proguard rules, native modules, signing config, dependency manifests and lockfiles.

artifact.description: Command(s) that build the release-form artifact exactly as shipped: shrinking, release signing and production config on.

flows.description: Named critical flows to exercise on that artifact, one evidence entry each.

device.description: Optional. Where to run it (an emulator image, a device, a staging host).

visualCheck.description: Per UI nature: how to run the live app for the owner's visual loop and what counts as visual evidence. Declaring it makes the nature a UI nature. Full rule: docs/visual-check.md.

run.description: Command(s) that start the live app with hot reload (the dev server).

open.description: How to open the dev client on the target: an emulator/device launch command or a browser URL.

devBuild.description: Command(s) that build and install the dev/debug client connected to the dev server; a release-form build cannot hot reload. Heavy work (docs/heavy-work.md).

profiles.description: Target device profiles the owner judges on, the owner's own first: resolution, density, font scale (include the largest), theme.

restore.description: Command(s) that put back the prior device values the loop recorded in state before changing them (wm size/density, font scale); also run on abort.

capture.description: Optional. Screenshot command for an unattended run (agent capture across every profile) or the PR record; writes to the state or scratch dir, never inside the repo, under a slugified profile name.

diff.description: Optional. Screenshot-diff harness against the base branch; run only when declared.

sharedPaths.description: Optional. Globs outside match whose change makes a visual confirmation stale (shared theme, i18n); added to match and the design.* paths in G11's staleness diff.

designTool.description: Optional. An installed design skill hooked into UI stages (e.g. impeccable); never required — adapter table in docs/visual-check.md.

bootCheck.description: Command(s) that load the FULL application context with EAGER bean creation (or boot to a health endpoint) — e.g. a @SpringBootTest(webEnvironment=NONE) context-load test selector. Declaring it marks the nature as context-bearing and makes gate G7b (sc-implement) required on every NON-inert change to the nature's production sources, catching framework-wiring breaks (a new type caught by an unchanged scan, bean-scope clashes, missing-property conditionals) that unit + sliced-IT + review all pass yet fail to boot. Prefer the cheap eager context-load kept as a standing suite test; an expensive full-server boot belongs in sc-qa (G9). Needs a full-context-capable env (a superset of the sliced ITs'). A selector matching zero tests is a misconfig FAIL, not a pass. Never wire an env-dependent boot into a CI path lacking its deps.

releaseChecklist.description: Optional. Release bookkeeping for projects that ship to a store, installer channel, registry or production host: version bump, third-party signing-key registration, release notes, backend-first deploy order, symbol/deobfuscation-map upload. Top-level, not per nature, because one release step often spans natures. sc-ship runs the items whose `when` matches right before G12: machine items (`manual` absent/false) run and are logged to the gate log; `manual: true` items go on the PR body's pre-merge manual gate. Not releaseSmoke (does the release artifact run, G9). Omit it and nothing changes. Evaluated from the base-branch copy of the overlay. Full rule: sc-ship — Release checklist.

id.description: Stable key, unique in the list; names the item in the gate log and the PR manual gate.

when.description: Selector; every key given must match (AND). Several items express OR.

changeNature.description: Matches when the change touches one of these changeNature names.

paths.description: Globs; matches when any changed path matches.

release.description: true: matches only when the PR base, as created or read from the host, equals vcs.releaseBranch (unset: never matches).

check.description: What to do or verify: a shell command for a machine item, prose for a `manual: true` item.

evidence.description: What counts as done: command exit status, a file present, or the human confirmation to record.

manual.description: true: a human must do it (a console, a store dashboard, a key registration). It is listed on the pre-merge manual gate and never run by the agent.

externalReviewers.description: Optional. Declares out-of-process review agents — a different model or CLI entirely — that a changeNature[].reviews entry may name, turning that lens into an ASYNC review job (§sc-review). The kit stays docs-only and never hard-codes a vendor: the project supplies every command. G8 then runs snapshot → launch → record the job in state.reviewJobs → the cycle may suspend and resume → judge on completion. A foreign reviewer is always an ADDITIONAL lens: it never replaces the in-session set, and a job that times out or fails does not lower G8's bar — it becomes a named deferral on the pre-merge manual gate.

$comment.description: Documentation only; not a reviewer. A reviewer cannot be named $comment.

launch.description: Command(s) that start the review and print a job id. Should be given the SNAPSHOT path, not the live branch — an out-of-process reader on a live branch forces a long git-write freeze, while a snapshot releases it in seconds.

status.description: Command(s) that report a job's state, given its id. Polled on the reviewer's own cadence; must distinguish running from a terminal state so G8 can tell 'not judged yet' from 'judged'.

fetch.description: Command(s) that retrieve a completed job's findings, given its id. Its output is judged like any other lens — same severity discipline, refutation pass and triage rubric.

cancel.description: Optional. Command(s) that stop a job, given its id. Used when G8 routes back to sc-implement and the in-flight review's subject is about to be rewritten — the job is recorded superseded, not waited out. Without it a superseded job is abandoned in state with its reason, never left silently running.

notify.description: Optional. Run once on the transition to a terminal state. Purely a convenience: /status already surfaces every reviewJobs entry, so completion is never dependent on this firing.

snapshot.description: Default true. Capture an immutable diff/bundle/detached-worktree at launch and hand the reviewer that instead of the live branch, so the git-write freeze releases as soon as it is written. Set false only for a reviewer that genuinely requires the live tree — then the freeze holds for the whole job and every stage that writes git must wait.

pollSeconds.description: How often to run the status command. Match the reviewer's real cadence; a 30-minute review does not need a 10-second poll.

maxWaitMinutes.description: Bounds the wait. On exceeding it the job is recorded status: timeout WITH ITS ID and carried to the pre-merge manual gate — never silently dropped, because 'the external reviewer timed out' must not become the standard way to ship without one.

effortMap.description: Maps the kit's effort levels onto whatever this host calls them, exactly as tierMap does for models. PREFLIGHT resolves per-stage effort into state.effort and every stage spawn passes it explicitly -- a default effort is the same silent override as a default model (Iron Law 6). Effort is priced on the judgment/mechanics axis, not on stage names: root-cause analysis and triage stay 'high' on every size tier, review effort scales with the size tier, and mechanics (setup, discovery, commit/push/PR, running tests, one-line edits) are 'low'. Absent this map, effort levels are advisory only.

securityReviewModel.description: Model id the 'security' and 'authz' review lenses MUST use, overriding their tier-resolved model. Set it when your top/high tier resolves to a model that refuses security analysis — such a review silently no-ops. Pin the most capable model that WILL do security review, at your HIGHEST security-review tier — note auth/payment risk upgrades that lens to 'top', and the pin overrides that upgrade too. Enforced when sc-review spawns those lenses; PREFLIGHT records it as models['review.security'] and logs SC-ROUTE-AVOID when the pin differs from the tier-resolved model. Opt-in: absent, the security lens uses its tier model.

reuseDevServer.description: Reuse an already-running dev server for QA. A bare port number, an object with an explicit health check, or true to auto-detect a running server.

oneOf.description: Auto-detect: reuse whatever dev server is already up.

sharedNodeModules.description: Share one dep store across worktrees (pnpm store or linked node_modules). The only env knob that is destructive on teardown: a linked node_modules must be swept for and unlinked before a worktree is deleted, or the delete reaches the shared store — see sc-ship Cleanup (G13) step 1.

heavyLock.description: Base path of the slot lock files (<path>.1..N) every one-shot heavy command (full test suite, release build) runs under, so sessions and worktrees serialize. Opt-in: absent, no serialization. See docs/heavy-work.md.

maxConcurrentHeavy.description: Heavy jobs allowed at once (N slot locks); effective value 1 when unset. Without heavyLock it only caps this orchestrator. See docs/heavy-work.md.

heavyHeadroomMB.description: Available memory (MB) required before launching a heavy job, with or without heavyLock; below it, wait or stop a job this session started. Opt-in, default off. See docs/heavy-work.md.
